newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bank shares rise on rate speculation.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bank shares rise on rate speculation.

text.p: Shares of major Canadian banks rose on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday on speculation that U.S. economic data due out on Friday would dampen speculation about U.S. rate rises in May.

Traders said concerns the Federal Reserve would raise U.S. rates at its Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20 subsided on speculation that U.S. payroll numbers for April would not appear to add to U.S. inflationary pressure.
"A lot of people just like to look at the immediate and I think they are going to suffer the consequences," said Roy Palmer, analyst with TD Securities Inc.
He said Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan had said repeatedly that monetary policy took six months to filter into the economy and that U.S. inflationary pressures continued to build in the United States.
A Reuter survey of economists forecast on average that U.S. payrolls in April rose 211,000, up from 175,000 in March.
The bank index in Toronto was up 1.59 percent or 108.01 to 6915.08.
Royal Bank of Canada was up 1.20 to 57.05, followed by Bank of Montreal up 1 to 51.70 and Bank of Nova Scotia up 1 to 54.05.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce rose 0.45 to 32.55, Toronto-Dominion Bank rose 0.50 to 40 and National Bank of Canada was up 0.15 to 16.45.
